successCriteria.description: The LeaveBalance model exposes the exact canonical field shape: id, employeeId, leaveTypeCode, periodStart, periodEnd, entitledDays, usedDays, pendingDays — no added, renamed, or omitted fields.
Opening an accrual period grants the FULL entitlement at period start with no pro-rata: entitledDays equals the policy's annualEntitlementDays, and usedDays and pendingDays are both 0.

Carry-forward on period close computes unused = entitledDays - usedDays - pendingDays, then carries min(unused, carryForwardDays) into the next period — a hard cap where days above the cap are forfeited.
src/modules/balance/index.ts publicly re-exports the LeaveBalance model, the repository interface and its Pg implementation, and the service interface and its implementation.

Jest unit tests under tests/unit/modules/balance/ cover accrual (full-entitlement grant, invalid input rejection, unknown employee/policy, duplicate key) and carry-forward (cap enforcement with forfeiture, zero carry, missing source, non-closable period).
The repository obtains its connection from the shared pool in src/shared/db/connection.ts and accepts an optional trailing PoolClient so it can join a caller's transaction.

constraints: LeaveTypeCode must be imported from src/shared/types/index.ts (not re-declared locally), and error types from src/shared/errors/index.ts.
The service owns the unit of work via an injected IUnitOfWork.withTransaction; it never imports a pool, client, or module-level db helper, and BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK are issued only by PgUnitOfWork.
All database access goes through the repository interface (GP-001); no inline SQL or direct pool access in the service.
Cross-module dependencies (employee, policy) are consumed only through their public index.ts entry points, never their internals.

Accrual and carry-forward are BINDING rules: full entitlement at period start (no pro-rata) and hard-cap carry-forward min(unused, carryForwardDays) with forfeiture above the cap — the implementation must not soften or reinterpret them.
Strict TypeScript: no `any` (use `unknown` with guards), no implicit any, strict null checks.
outOfScope: HTTP routes, controllers, and RBAC guards for the balance module — deferred to the leave orchestrator phase; this phase is service/repository/model only.
Audit-log writes (GP-002) for balance state changes — the leave orchestrator owns audit/notification side effects; balance does not write audit rows in this phase.
Pro-rata accrual, monthly installments, and any accrual model other than full-entitlement-at-period-start.
BullMQ / background accrual schedulers and notification fanout — accrual and carry-forward are invoked synchronously by the service.
Knex migrations / DDL for the leave_balances table — persistence schema work is not part of this phase.

entityInvariants.invariant: A balance is uniquely identified per employee + leaveTypeCode + accrual period (periodStart/periodEnd); at most one row may exist for a given key, and a duplicate create is rejected with ConflictError.
OPEN vs CLOSED is not a stored field — it is inferred from periodStart/periodEnd relative to the current date; a period whose periodEnd is in the future is not closable.
Day counters are non-negative and consistent: entitledDays >= 0, usedDays >= 0, pendingDays >= 0, and unused = entitledDays - usedDays - pendingDays must not be negative.
On open, entitledDays equals the policy's annualEntitlementDays (full grant, no pro-rata) and usedDays/pendingDays start at 0.
On carry-forward, the next period's entitledDays gains exactly min(unused, carryForwardDays); days above the cap are forfeited and never added.

interfaceConstraints.operation: openPeriod (open an accrual period / grant entitlement)
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: ValidationError(400) on invalid input (empty employeeId, invalid LeaveTypeCode, invalid dates, periodStart >= periodEnd, non-positive entitlement); NotFoundError(404) on unknown employee or missing policy; ConflictError(409) on duplicate balance key.

interfaceConstraints.operation: carryForward (close a period and roll unused days into the next)
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: NotFoundError(404) on missing source balance; ValidationError(400) when the source period is not closable (periodEnd in the future) or counters are negative.
NotFoundError(404) on unknown balance id; read-only, never opens a transaction or forwards a client.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: LeaveTypeCode enum must be the one from shared types (lowercase persisted values annual/sick/emergency/unpaid/maternity/paternity), not a local re-declaration.
Error types (ValidationError, NotFoundError, ConflictError) must be the shared AppError subclasses with their canonical status codes, not local error classes.

The transaction boundary must match IUnitOfWork.withTransaction semantics: service owns the unit of work, data-access opens it, repositories take an optional trailing PoolClient and fall back to the shared pool.
Entitlement and carry-forward cap must be resolved from the live LeavePolicy fields annualEntitlementDays, accrualPeriodMonths, and carryForwardDays via IPolicyService.getPolicyByLeaveTypeCode.
Employee existence must be verified via IEmployeeService.getEmployeeById (cross-module dependency through the public entry point).
The repository must obtain its connection from the shared pool, matching the existing connection module.

integrationPoints.why: Resolves annualEntitlementDays, accrualPeriodMonths, and carryForwardDays that drive the binding accrual and carry-forward rules.
Verifies the employee exists before opening a balance period.
Provides the transaction boundary the service uses to make openPeriod/carryForward atomic.
Canonical leave-type enum used as the balance's leaveTypeCode discriminator.
Typed error semantics for invalid input, missing entities, and duplicate keys.
